_comment_family: The family name straight out of the file's name table (ID 1), and it
is safe to ask for by family alone here in the way Bebas Neue's is
and Telegraf's is not: the app carries one cut of League Spartan.
There is no second weight sharing the name for a request to land on
by accident, so 'League Spartan' can only ever be this file's
That is a fact about what is in fonts/ rather than about the family.
League Spartan ships upstream as a variable face running 100 to 900,
and the day a second cut is dropped in beside this one the two Telegraf
packs are the pattern to follow: each declares its own full name, so
neither can answer to the other's request.
Weight 400, which is what the file's OS/2 table says and what its
subfamily (ID 2) calls it. Asking for anything else here would invite
a browser to synthesise a weight this file does not contain, and a
synthesised weight is measured as well as drawn - the caption would be
laid out against letters nobody chose.
_comment_css: Not declared in styles.css. This face arrived with a channel and is
registered from this JSON at load time (see registerFace in
js/channels.js), which is the route content/README.md describes -
nothing has to be added to the stylesheet for it.
_comment_local: What the machine may already know the face by, tried after the file
and used by the installer as the name it registers this face under
The PostScript name first, then the Windows full name, then the
family. The family is included, unlike in the Telegraf packs, for the
reason given above: it names one cut here because there is only one,
so a machine answering to it is answering with these letterforms.
_comment_stack: The fallbacks are damage limitation and never a design choice - a
title laid out against the wrong metrics is broken rather than merely
different, which is what fontguard exists to catch before anything is
drawn. Chosen all the same: League Spartan is a geometric sans built
on the circle, so the nearest thing a Windows machine can be relied on
to have is Century Gothic, with Segoe UI behind it for the machine
Impact and Arial Black are absent for garet-book's reason - they are
heavy display cuts, and putting one behind a 400-weight geometric
would make the one thing that survives a missing file the furthest
